rationale: Independent reading: held EO 9380 (8 FR 13081, Sept. 25, 1943; paras. 1-3 on p. 13081, paras. 3-7 on p. 13083 of the held extract) establishes the Foreign Economic Administration (para. 1), consolidates four offices into it (2), lets the Administrator organize it (3), sets its policy conformity and liberated-areas role (4), transfers personnel and funds to it (5), restricts the Administrator's use of Pub. L. 139 funds (6), and amends conflicting orders / sets effectiveness (7). Every continuing provision operates through the FEA or its Administrator. Held EO 9630 (10 FR 12245, Sept. 27, 1945) Part I para. 1: 'The Foreign Economic Administration established by Executive Order No. 9380 ... and the office of the Administrator ... are terminated', with paras. 2-5 redistributing all its functions to State, RFC, Commerce and Agriculture and para. 4(d) giving Commerce the final liquidation. Termination of the sole entity and office through which the order operates ends the whole order: my independent status NO, agreeing with the producer (cf. Bowditch EO 9204). D6: was any later event that ended or changed this clause removed or ignored? Considered and not ignored: EO 9385 (1943) is an earlier amendment adding food functions; EO 10945 (May 24, 1961) sec. 5(a)(5) supersedes 'all provisions relating to export control that are contained in [EO 9380] and are now effective'. That 1961 clause is a conditional cleanup formula ('are now effective') and the export-control function had already been moved out of the terminated FEA to Commerce by EO 9630 Part I para. 4(a); it does not show any EO 9380 provision continuing as an operating norm, and nothing restores the FEA. The producer addressed EO 10945 explicitly. Non-fatal residual noted for the owner: a stricter convention could date the last vestige (export-control consolidation via para. 2) to 1961 rather than 1945; either way the status is NO. Accept as a provisional NO hypothesis (end on or before Sept. 27, 1945, with the EO 10945 caveat).
